facts.fact: The Department of Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation says the Presidential Hotline received 339,579 cases since September 2009, including calls, emails and walk-ins, of which 242,636 were complaints, logged in a web-based ITSM system.
DPME says hotline complaints are assigned through ITSM directly to stakeholders, municipalities and departments, each with a licence to view and close cases.
DPME says 234,752 of 242,636 complaints (96.7%) were resolved as at 17 December 2024 and that quarterly, mid-year and annual hotline reports are available.
DPME says the Khawuleza app received no cases after being piloted in Limpopo owing to technical glitches, and benchmarking is under way for digitalising the hotline.

note: Hotline is calls, mail and walk-ins; a task team only studies a future digitalised system, no digital channel stated.
Real411 takes disinformation complaints, not complaints about public services.
The OCPO complaints portal is for procurement grievances to the treasury office, with no case figures or public-services reach stated.
Explains petitions to Parliament; no government complaint channel on public services stated.

facts.fact: The Minister's reply says the Presidential Hotline received 1,832 complaints in the first quarter of 2025/26.
The reply says national and provincial departments are expected to resolve complaints assigned to them by the Presidential Hotline within 25 working days.
The reply says 991 of 1,832 complaints were resolved in the first quarter of 2025/26, a 55 per cent resolution rate.
